description: This Dart source file defines the 'LocalDb' class, a singleton interface for managing a local SQLite database in a Flutter application. It handles database creation, schema migrations, and provides methods for managing user session data, attendance records, and pending synchronization queue entries. The class includes schema versioning with support for migrations from schema version 1 to 3, and defines tables like 'users', 'attendance', and 'pending_sync'.

classes.name: LocalDb
classes.description: A singleton class providing an interface to a local SQLite database for storing user sessions, attendance, and sync queue data.

methods.name: init
methods.description: Initializes the database, creates schema, and applies migrations if needed.

methods.name: _createV1
methods.description: Creates the initial database schema for version 1.

methods.name: _migrateToV2
methods.description: Migrates database schema from version 1 to version 2 by adding new columns.

methods.name: _migrateToV3
methods.description: Migrates database schema from version 2 to version 3, for example adding more columns.

methods.name: _migrate
methods.description: Handles incremental migration logic based on old and new schema versions.

methods.name: insertUser
methods.description: Inserts or replaces the current user record, maintaining a single-row user model.

methods.name: getUser
methods.description: Retrieves the current user data if exists.

methods.name: clearUser
methods.description: Deletes all user entries, effectively logging out.

methods.name: addAttendance
methods.description: Adds an attendance record with optional student name, period, notes.

methods.name: getDaily
methods.description: Retrieves attendance records for a specific date.

methods.name: getWeekly
methods.description: Retrieves attendance records within a start and end date range.

methods.name: queuePending
methods.description: Queues a payload (as JSON) for later synchronization.

methods.name: getPending
methods.description: Retrieves all pending sync payloads ordered by creation time.
